title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1969-03-02
source: Bertha Remaster of the Multi-Track source.

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a raw ’69 marathon that opens with a blazing Dark Star and delivers an epic Alligator jam.
ai_review.review: The reviewer raves about the show’s relentless improvisation – from a psychedelic Dark Star into St. Stephen, The Eleven and Lovelight, through a furious Cryptical→Other One sequence, to a massive Alligator jam that feels like pure early‑Dead fire. The soundboard source is praised for its clarity with only a brief cut at the end of Goodnight, making the recording as compelling as the performance.

ai_rating.rationale: Single five‑star review emphasizes an outstanding performance and a clean soundboard source; rating reflects strong show quality with minor recording blemish.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, well‑balanced mix; only noted a small cut on the Goodnight ending, otherwise crisp and immersive.

standout_songs: Dark Star > St. Stephen > The Eleven > Lovelight
show_quality.setlist_flow: The concert bursts open with a monumental Dark Star, maintaining high‑energy improvisation throughout both sets and closing on an understated Goodnight that leaves the audience floating.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s lead work is highlighted as “nailed” on Death Don’t and dominates the Alligator jam.
band_member_comments.Phil: Described as ever‑present, providing a strong backbone especially in The Eleven and the extended jams.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keyboard work called very psychedelic; reviewer debates whether Tom Constanten or Pigpen is playing, leaning toward Tom’s classical fugue style.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mentions “drummers” adding to the heavy jam sections, implying solid rhythmic support.
